question: Who among the following won the Best Music Director award at the 67th National Film Award Ceremony?
solution_text:
The correct answer is D. Imman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• D. Imman won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction at the 67th National Film Awards (for films of 2019, ceremony held in 2021) for his work in the Tamil film Comali. (डी. इम्मान — सर्वश्रेष्ठ संगीत निर्देशन)

 

• With this award, he became one of the few Tamil music composers to win this honour, recognised for blending folk and contemporary musical styles.

 

• The National Film Awards are presented annually by the Directorate of Film Festivals, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, and are among the most prestigious film honours in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 67th National Film Awards' Best Feature Film award went to Marakkar: Arabikadalinte Simham (Malayalam).

 

• Best Actor and Best Actress awards at the 67th National Film Awards went to Dhanush (Asuran) and Kangana Ranaut (Manikarnika and Panga), respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopi Sundar (Option 1): Noted Malayalam-Telugu-Tamil film composer, but did not win this particular award.

 

• Mani Sharma (Option 3): Veteran Telugu film composer, not the winner of this award at the 67th ceremony.

 

• Devi Sri Prasad (Option 4): Popular Telugu film composer, not the winner of this award at the 67th ceremony.

question: ______ are known as narrow money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is M1 and M2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the RBI's monetary aggregates classification, M1 and M2 are together known as "narrow money", while M3 and M4 are known as "broad money". (संकीर्ण मुद्रा — M1 और M2)

 

• M1 = Currency with the public + Demand deposits with banks + Other deposits with the RBI.

 

• M2 = M1 + Savings deposits of post office savings banks.

 

• Narrow money aggregates (M1, M2) consist of highly liquid assets that can be readily used as a medium of exchange.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• M3 (Broad Money) = M1 + Time deposits with banks; this is the most commonly used measure of money supply in India.

 

• M4 = M3 + Total deposits with post office savings organisations (excluding National Savings Certificates).

 

NOTE

 

• M2 and M4 (Option 2): Incorrect combination; M2 is part of narrow money but M4 is part of broad money.

 

• M3 and M2 (Option 3): Incorrect combination; M3 is broad money, not narrow money.

 

• M1 and M4 (Option 4): Incorrect combination; M1 is narrow money but M4 is broad money.

question: Samudragupta’s mother belonged to which of the following gana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lichchhavi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Samudragupta's mother, Kumaradevi, belonged to the Lichchhavi gana (clan), an ancient republican clan of Vaishali. (कुमारदेवी — लिच्छवि गण)

 

• Samudragupta's father, Chandragupta I, married Kumaradevi, and this matrimonial alliance with the Lichchhavis is believed to have significantly strengthened the political and territorial standing of the early Gupta dynasty.

 

• Some Gupta coins bear the legend "Lichchhavayah", and Samudragupta himself is referred to as "Lichchhavi-dauhitra" (daughter's son of the Lichchhavis) in inscriptions, highlighting the importance of this lineage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lichchhavis were one of the leading clans of the Vajji Mahajanapada, with their capital at Vaishali, and are also associated with being one of the earliest known republics in world history.

 

• Chandragupta I is regarded as the first sovereign ruler of the Gupta dynasty and is believed to have started the Gupta Era (319-320 CE).

 

NOTE

 

• Koliya (Option 1): A republican clan associated with the region of Ramagrama, related by marriage to the Sakyas.

 

• Sakya (Option 3): The clan to which Gautama Buddha belonged, with capital at Kapilavastu.

 

• Vajji (Option 4): A confederacy of clans (including the Lichchhavis) forming one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, not Samudragupta's maternal gana specifically.

question: Padma Subrahmanyam is the exponent of which of the following Indian dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Padma Subrahmanyam is a renowned exponent, scholar and choreographer of Bharatanatyam, the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu. (पद्मा सुब्रह्मण्यम — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She developed the dance technique known as "Bharatanrityam", which incorporates elements from ancient Tamil dance traditions and Bharata's Natyashastra.

 

• She has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, and is a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy, and Alarmel Valli.

 

• Bharatanatyam is characterised by fixed upper torso, bent legs and knees flexed (araimandi), combined with intricate footwork and a sophisticated vocabulary of gestures (mudras).

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): Classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): Classical dance form of North India, associated with exponents like Birju Maharaj.

 

• Mohiniattam (Option 4): Classical dance form of Kerala, a graceful, feminine solo dance style.

question: The crust is the Earth's outermost layer that is less than _______ percent of Earth by mass, with oceanic crust and continental crust often consisting of more felsic rocks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The crust is the Earth's thin, outermost solid layer and accounts for less than 1 percent of Earth's total mass, even though it forms the surface we live on. (भूपर्पटी — पृथ्वी के द्रव्यमान का 1% से कम)

 

• The crust is divided into oceanic crust (thinner, denser, mainly basaltic/mafic) and continental crust (thicker, lighter, mainly granitic/felsic in composition).

 

• Beneath the crust lies the mantle, which makes up the bulk (about 84%) of Earth's volume and a large share of its mass, followed by the core at the centre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Oceanic crust is typically 5-10 km thick, while continental crust is much thicker, averaging 30-50 km (up to ~70 km under high mountain ranges like the Himalayas).

 

• The boundary between the crust and the mantle is known as the Mohorovicic Discontinuity (Moho).

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 1):, 2 (Option 3): and 10 (Option 4): all overstate the crust's share of Earth's mass; the crust's actual contribution is less than 1 percent.

question: Which of the following jurisdictions of the Supreme Court allows it to settle disputes between the centre and state and amongst states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Original.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under its Original Jurisdiction (Article 131 of the Constitution), the Supreme Court of India has exclusive power to settle disputes between the Centre and one or more states, and among states themselves. (मूल क्षेत्राधिकार — अनुच्छेद 131)

 

• Such disputes must involve a question of law or fact on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends; the Supreme Court is the court of first instance for such cases, not an appellate forum.

 

• This jurisdiction excludes disputes arising from treaties, agreements or similar instruments made before the Constitution came into force, which are expressly kept outside the scope of Article 131.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Supreme Court's Appellate Jurisdiction (Articles 132-136) allows it to hear appeals from High Courts in constitutional, civil, and criminal matters.

 

• Its Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143) allows the President to seek the Court's opinion on questions of law or fact of public importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Appellate (Option 1): Relates to hearing appeals against High Court judgments, not centre-state disputes.

 

• Advisory (Option 2): Relates to giving opinions to the President on referred questions, not settling disputes.

 

• Writ (Option 3): Relates to the power to issue writs (Article 32) for enforcement of fundamental rights, not centre-state disputes.

question: Cells of meristematci tissue lack ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vacuoles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meristematic tissue cells are actively dividing cells found at the growing regions of plants; they are characterised by having dense cytoplasm and lacking large vacuoles. (विभज्योतक ऊतक — रिक्तिकाओं का अभाव)

 

• These cells are typically thin-walled, compactly arranged with no intercellular spaces, and possess a prominent nucleus, all features suited to rapid cell division and growth.

 

• Meristematic tissue is classified based on location into apical (at root and shoot tips), lateral (cambium), and intercalary (at the base of leaves/internodes) meristems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cells produced by meristems later differentiate into permanent tissues — simple (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex (xylem, phloem).

 

NOTE

 

• Cellulose wall (Option 1): Meristematic cells do have thin cellulose cell walls; this is not something they lack.

 

• Cytoplasm (Option 3): Meristematic cells have dense, abundant cytoplasm; they do not lack it.

 

• Nuclei (Option 4): Meristematic cells have a large, prominent nucleus; they do not lack it.

question: The upper portion of the mantle is called ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is asthenosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The asthenosphere is the upper, semi-molten (plastic/ductile) layer of the mantle, lying just beneath the rigid lithosphere, extending roughly from about 80 km to 200 km in depth. (दुर्बलतामंडल — मैंटल की ऊपरी परत)

 

• Because it is weak and can slowly flow, the asthenosphere allows the rigid tectonic plates of the lithosphere above it to move, making it central to the theory of plate tectonics.

 

• It is largely responsible for isostatic adjustments and magma generation that feeds volcanic activity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The lithosphere comprises the crust and the uppermost rigid part of the mantle, and is broken into tectonic plates that float on the asthenosphere.

 

• Below the asthenosphere lies the more rigid mesosphere (lower mantle), which extends down to the outer core.

 

NOTE

 

• Lithosphere (Option 1): The rigid outer shell comprising the crust and topmost mantle, not the semi-fluid upper mantle layer described here.

 

• Stratosphere (Option 2): A layer of Earth's atmosphere, unrelated to the mantle.

 

• Mesosphere (Option 3): Refers either to a lower atmospheric layer or, in geology, to the more rigid lower mantle, not the upper mantle.

question: Guru Purnima, a festival celebrated by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists in India falls in which month of Hindu calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashadha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Purnima is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the Hindu month of Ashadha, usually falling in June-July of the Gregorian calendar. (गुरु पूर्णिमा — आषाढ़ मास)

 

• The festival is dedicated to honouring one's teachers and spiritual guides; Hindus associate it with sage Ved Vyasa, the compiler of the Vedas, while Buddhists associate it with Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath.

 

• Jains observe it as the day Lord Mahavira made his first disciple, Gautam Swami, marking the start of the monastic order.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashadha Purnima is also known as Vyasa Purnima, in reverence to Ved Vyasa.

 

• Other notable Purnima festivals include Kartik Purnima (Kartika month) and Buddha Purnima (Vaisakha month).

 

NOTE

 

• Kartika (Option 1): Associated with Kartik Purnima / Dev Diwali, not Guru Purnima.

 

• Vaisakha (Option 2): Associated with Buddha Purnima (Buddha's birth), not Guru Purnima.

 

• Sravana (Option 3): Associated with festivals like Raksha Bandhan and Nag Panchami, not Guru Purnima.

question: In May 2022, the Inter-State Council, which works to promote and support cooperative federalism in the country, has been reconstituted. Who will be the chairman of this council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Inter-State Council was set up under Article 263 of the Constitution to facilitate coordination between the Centre and states (and among states) and is chaired by the Prime Minister of India. (अंतर्राज्यीय परिषद — प्रधानमंत्री अध्यक्ष)

 

• In May 2022, the Council was reconstituted with the Prime Minister as Chairman, all Chief Ministers of states, Administrators/Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories (without a legislature), and Union Cabinet Ministers as invited members.

 

• The Council was established in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission (1988), which was set up to review Centre-State relations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Inter-State Council Secretariat, headquartered in New Delhi, also serves as the secretariat for the Zonal Councils.

 

• There are five Zonal Councils in India — Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western and Central — each also chaired by the Union Home Minister as vice-chairman in practice.

 

NOTE

 

• President of India (Option 1): Not the chairman of the Inter-State Council.

 

• Chief Justice of India (Option 2): Heads the judiciary, unrelated to the Inter-State Council.

 

• Finance minister of India (Option 4): Not the chairman of the Inter-State Council; the Finance Minister is instead a member.

question: Which of the following festivals is mainly celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Solung.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Solung is a major harvest festival celebrated mainly by the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, usually in the first week of September. (सोलुंग महोत्सव — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It marks the end of the sowing season and involves community feasts, folk dances like Ponung, and rituals for a good harvest and protection of crops and livestock.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh celebrates several other tribal festivals as well, including Losar (Monpa) and Mopin (Galo).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arunachal Pradesh is home to numerous tribes, and its festivals largely revolve around agricultural cycles and community harmony.

 

NOTE

 

• Hornbill (Option 1): Flagship cultural festival of Nagaland, held annually from 1-10 December at Kisama.

 

• Ambubachi (Option 2): Celebrated at the Kamakhya Temple in Assam, associated with the menstruation of the goddess.

 

• Wangala (Option 3): Post-harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, also called the "festival of a hundred drums".

question: The poverty ratio has declined to ______ in 2011-12 in Urban India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26.4 percent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Rangarajan Committee methodology for poverty estimation, the urban poverty ratio in India declined to 26.4 percent in 2011-12. (रंगराजन समिति — शहरी निर्धनता अनुपात 26.4%)

 

• The same report estimated the rural poverty ratio at 30.9 percent and the all-India (combined) poverty ratio at 29.5 percent for 2011-12.

 

• The Rangarajan Committee, headed by economist C. Rangarajan, was constituted in 2012 to review the poverty line methodology used by the earlier Tendulkar Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The earlier Tendulkar Committee methodology had estimated a lower urban poverty figure (13.7 percent) for 2011-12, using a different consumption-based poverty line.

 

• The Rangarajan Committee report was submitted in 2014 and proposed higher monthly per capita consumption expenditure thresholds than the Tendulkar methodology.

 

NOTE

 

• 21.4 percent (Option 1), 23.4 percent (Option 3) and 28.4 percent (Option 4) are close but incorrect figures; the Rangarajan Committee's actual urban poverty estimate for 2011-12 was 26.4 percent.

question: At which of the following places was the FIFA Men's World Cup, held in 2018?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Russia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2018 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Russia, held from 14 June to 15 July 2018 across 11 host cities. (फीफा विश्व कप 2018 — रूस)

 

• The tournament was won by France, who defeated Croatia 4-2 in the final held at the Luzhniki Stadium, Moscow.

 

• Luka Modric (Croatia) won the Golden Ball (best player), and Harry Kane (England) won the Golden Boot (top scorer) at this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• It was the first FIFA World Cup held in Eastern Europe and the first hosted by a former Soviet Union country.

 

• The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar, and the 2026 FIFA World Cup is scheduled to be jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico.

 

NOTE

 

• China (Option 2), Turkey (Option 3) and Columbia (Option 4): None of these countries have hosted a FIFA Men's World Cup to date.

question: In which year, James Mill Published a massive three-volume work, “A History of British India”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1817.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• James Mill, a Scottish historian, economist and philosopher, published his massive three-volume work "The History of British India" in 1817. (जेम्स मिल — 1817 में प्रकाशित)

 

• In this work, Mill divided Indian history into three periods — Hindu civilisation, Muslim civilisation, and the British period — a periodisation later criticised by historians for being communally biased and Eurocentric.

 

• Mill wrote the book without ever visiting India, relying instead on official records and secondary sources available in Britain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• James Mill later served in the British East India Company, eventually rising to the position of Chief Examiner.

 

• His son, John Stuart Mill, was a celebrated philosopher and economist who also worked with the East India Company.

 

NOTE

 

• 1815 (Option 1), 1807 (Option 2) and 1805 (Option 3): None of these correspond to the actual year of publication, which was 1817.

question: The ISSF Junior World Cup 2022 was held in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Germany.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ISSF Junior World Cup (Rifle/Pistol) 2022 was held in Suhl, Germany, in July 2022. (आईएसएसएफ जूनियर विश्व कप 2022 — जर्मनी)

 

• Indian shooters, including Esha Singh, delivered strong performances at this edition, winning multiple medals across rifle and pistol events.

 

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) organises World Cups and Junior World Cups across rifle, pistol and shotgun disciplines every year in different host countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Suhl in Germany, home to the Schießsportzentrum Suhl shooting sport centre, has hosted several ISSF junior events over the years.

 

• India has emerged as one of the strongest nations in junior-level shooting competitions in recent years, regularly finishing among the top medal-winning countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Iran (Option 2), Turkey (Option 3) and UAE (Option 4): None of these were hosts of the 2022 ISSF Junior World Cup (Rifle/Pistol) referred to here.

question: How many delegates attended the first session of Congress in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 72.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, and was attended by 72 delegates. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — प्रथम अधिवेशन, 72 प्रतिनिधि)

 

• The session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and was organised under the guidance of Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant.

 

• The Indian National Congress was originally conceived, in part, as a "safety valve" to channel growing political discontent among educated Indians into constitutional means.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The second session of the Congress (1886) was held in Calcutta under the presidency of Dadabhai Naoroji, with a much larger attendance.

 

• The INC went on to become the principal vehicle of India's freedom struggle over the following decades.

 

NOTE

 

• 62 (Option 1), 78 (Option 2) and 68 (Option 3): None of these match the actual number of delegates (72) at the first INC session.

question: Effect of The Industrial Policy, 1956 on industries was _____.
option_2: India become self-sufficient in industrial goods
option_3: imports of those goods which could be produced in India itself was avoided
option_4: industries share fell in the GDP during 1991
solution_text:
The correct answer is industries started to get diversified.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1956, based on the goal of a "socialistic pattern of society", classified industries into three categories (public sector, mixed public-private, and private sector) and gave a strong push to setting up a wide range of new industries. (औद्योगिक नीति 1956 — उद्योगों का विविधीकरण)

 

• As a direct effect of this policy, India's industrial base diversified significantly, with new heavy, basic and capital-goods industries (steel, machine tools, power equipment, etc.) being established, particularly in the public sector.

 

• The policy gave the state a dominant role in the economy, reserving key and strategic industries exclusively for the public sector while permitting private enterprise in the remaining areas under regulation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPR 1956 is often called the "Economic Constitution of India" because it laid the framework for India's industrial development for decades, until the 1991 economic liberalisation reforms.

 

• It followed the earlier Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948, which had first outlined the role of the state in India's post-independence industrial economy.

 

NOTE

 

• India become self-sufficient in industrial goods (Option 2): India did not become fully self-sufficient in industrial goods purely as a result of the 1956 policy.

 

• Imports of those goods which could be produced in India itself was avoided (Option 3): Import substitution was a broader long-term economic strategy, not the direct, defining effect of the 1956 policy alone.

 

• Industries share fell in the GDP during 1991 (Option 4): This is unrelated to the 1956 policy; if anything, the industrial share of GDP was a later, separate economic trend tied to the 1991 reforms.

question: Which of the following revolutionary groups’ members assassinated Assistant Superintendent of Police John Saunders in 1927?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustan Republican Association.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assistant Superintendent of Police John Saunders was shot dead at Lahore (on 17 December 1928) by revolutionaries Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Chandrashekhar Azad, avenging the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. (जॉन सॉन्डर्स हत्या — हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन)

 

• These revolutionaries belonged to the organisation founded as the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) in 1924 by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Chandrashekhar Azad and others.

 

• The HRA was later reorganised and renamed the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928, under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh, with an expanded socialist ideology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same group of revolutionaries later carried out the Central Assembly Bombing (1929) in Delhi, led by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai died in 1928 from injuries sustained during a lathi charge while protesting against the Simon Commission, which triggered the plot to avenge his death.

 

NOTE

 

• Hindustan Sewa Dal (Option 1): Not the organisation associated with the Saunders assassination.

 

• Abhinav Bharat Secret Society (Option 3): A secret society founded by V. D. Savarkar in Maharashtra, unrelated to the Saunders case.

 

• Anushilan Samiti (Option 4): A revolutionary organisation based mainly in Bengal, not directly responsible for the Saunders assassination.

question: What is the correct percentage by volume of various gases in Earth's atmosphere?
option_1: 20.95% nitrogen, 78.09% oxygen, and 0.04% carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases.
option_2: 10.95%nitrogen, 88.09% oxygen, and 0.09% carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases.
option_3: 10.95% nitrogen, 78.09% oxygen, and 0.03% carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases.
option_4: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 0.03% carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 0.03% carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Earth's atmosphere by volume is composed of approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and roughly 0.03-0.04% carbon dioxide along with other trace and greenhouse gases (including about 0.93% argon). (पृथ्वी का वायुमंडल — 78% नाइट्रोजन, 21% ऑक्सीजन)

 

• Nitrogen (N₂) is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, followed by oxygen (O₂), which is essential for respiration and combustion.

 

• Carbon dioxide, though present only in trace amounts, plays a critical role in the greenhouse effect and photosynthesis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Argon (about 0.93%) is the third most abundant gas in the atmosphere, followed by trace amounts of neon, helium, methane, krypton, hydrogen and ozone.

 

• Rising atmospheric CO₂ concentration (currently above 400 parts per million) due to human activity is a major driver of global warming and climate change.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrectly swaps the percentages of nitrogen and oxygen (nitrogen should be the larger figure, ~78%, not oxygen).

 

• Option 2: States implausible values (10.95% nitrogen, 88.09% oxygen), which do not reflect the actual atmospheric composition.

 

• Option 3: Also swaps nitrogen and oxygen incorrectly and understates nitrogen's share.

question:
The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 prohibits which of the following activities in Antarctica?

I. Nuclear explosion

II. Introduction of non-sterile soil

III. Discharge of garbage
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II and III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 prohibits a range of harmful activities in Antarctica, including nuclear explosions, introduction of non-sterile soil, and discharge of garbage, plastic or other waste into the Antarctic environment. (भारतीय अंटार्कटिक विधेयक 2022 — सभी तीन गतिविधियाँ निषिद्ध)

 

• The Bill gives effect to India's obligations under the Antarctic Treaty (1959), the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty (Madrid Protocol, 1991), and the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

 

• It establishes a Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection to regulate Indian activities (including tourism and research) in Antarctica and provides for penalties for violations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently operates two research stations in Antarctica — Maitri and Bharati — and previously operated Dakshin Gangotri, its first station (now defunct/buried in ice).

 

• India acceded to the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and has been conducting scientific expeditions to Antarctica since 1981.

 

NOTE

 

• I and II (Option 1), Only III (Option 3) and II and III (Option 4): Each of these leaves out at least one activity (nuclear explosion, introduction of non-sterile soil, or discharge of garbage) that is, in fact, prohibited under the Bill.

question: In organic chemistry, which of the following is an empirical rule used to predict the regioselectivity of electrophilic addition reactions of alkanes and alkynes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Markovnikov’s rule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Markovnikov's rule is an empirical rule stating that in the electrophilic addition of a protic acid (HX) to an unsymmetrical alkene or alkyne, the hydrogen atom becomes attached to the carbon with the greater number of hydrogen substituents, while the halide/electrophile attaches to the more substituted carbon. (मार्कोवनिकोव नियम — इलेक्ट्रोफिलिक योगात्मक अभिक्रिया)

 

• It was formulated by Russian chemist Vladimir Markovnikov in 1869 and is widely used to predict the major product (regioselectivity) of such addition reactions.

 

• The rule is explained on the basis of the relative stability of the carbocation intermediate formed during the reaction — the more stable (more substituted) carbocation is favoured.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reverse selectivity, called "anti-Markovnikov" addition, occurs in the presence of peroxides during HBr addition, known as the Kharasch effect (peroxide effect).

 

NOTE

 

• Cornforth's rules (Option 1): Relate to stereochemical models used to predict the outcome of nucleophilic addition to carbonyl compounds, not this type of regioselectivity.

 

• Bredt's rule (Option 2): States that bridgehead carbons in small bicyclic systems generally cannot bear a double bond, unrelated to this rule.

 

• Baldwin's rules (Option 4): A set of guidelines predicting the favourability of ring-closure (cyclisation) reactions, not electrophilic addition regioselectivity.

question: Which crop does not require high rainfall and high temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maize.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maize is a versatile crop that can be grown in a wide range of climatic conditions and does not require particularly high rainfall or high temperature, unlike rice or jute; it thrives with moderate rainfall (about 50-100 cm) and moderate temperatures (21-27°C). (मक्का — मध्यम वर्षा और तापमान में उगने वाली फसल)

 

• It is grown as both a kharif and, in some regions, a rabi crop, and is cultivated widely across states like Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Its adaptability to diverse soil and climate conditions makes maize one of the most widely distributed cereal crops in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Maize is used both as a food grain and as fodder, and is also a major raw material for starch, corn oil and ethanol production.

 

NOTE

 

• Rice (Option 1): A kharif crop that needs high rainfall (over 100 cm) and high temperature, typically grown in areas of assured irrigation or heavy monsoon rainfall.

 

• Jute (Option 2): Requires high temperature and high humidity/rainfall, grown mainly in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region (West Bengal).

 

• Cotton (Option 4): A kharif crop requiring high temperature throughout its growing period, along with at least moderate rainfall or irrigation.

question: India’s first Olympic Values Education Programme (OVEP) was launched in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first Olympic Values Education Programme (OVEP) was launched in Odisha, in collaboration with the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), and the Abhinav Bindra Foundation Trust (ABFT). (ओलंपिक मूल्य शिक्षा कार्यक्रम — ओडिशा में शुभारंभ)

 

• The programme was launched by Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and was rolled out as a pilot project in Odisha's schools to teach values such as excellence, friendship and respect through sport.

 

• Odisha has actively positioned itself as a hub for sports development in India, also hosting major international events like the Hockey World Cup and the Men's FIH Hockey World Cup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Abhinav Bindra Foundation Trust was set up by India's first individual Olympic gold medallist, Abhinav Bindra, to promote sports development and athlete welfare in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1), Punjab (Option 2) and Haryana (Option 4): None of these states hosted the launch of India's first OVEP project; it was launched in Odisha.

question: According to Article 51 A (a) of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every Indian citizen to abide by the ___________ and respect its ideals and institutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(a) of the Indian Constitution, part of the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA), states that it is the duty of every citizen of India "to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem." (मौलिक कर्तव्य — संविधान का पालन)

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added; an 11th duty (regarding the duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by Article 51A largely modelled on similar provisions in the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable by courts, though they serve as a constant reminder to citizens.

 

NOTE

 

• Secularism (Option 2), Socialism (Option 3) and Democracy (Option 4): These are values/principles embedded elsewhere in the Constitution (notably in the Preamble), but Article 51A(a) specifically refers to abiding by the Constitution.

question: In which of the following states of India is “MANAS” biosphere Reserve located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Manas Biosphere Reserve is located in the state of Assam, along the India-Bhutan border, spread across the foothills of the Himalayas. (मानस जैवमंडल रिज़र्व — असम)

 

• It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a Project Tiger Reserve, an Elephant Reserve, and a designated Important Bird Area, known for its rich biodiversity including the Assam roofed turtle, pygmy hog, and golden langur.

 

• The reserve derives its name from the Manas River, a major tributary of the Brahmaputra that flows through it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Assam is home to several other important protected areas, including Kaziranga National Park (famous for the one-horned rhinoceros) and Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve.

 

• India currently has 18 Biosphere Reserves, of which several (including Manas) are also recognised under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura (Option 1), Manipur (Option 2) and Meghalaya (Option 3): None of these states host the Manas Biosphere Reserve, which is located in Assam.
